text: The Second Law of Thermodynamics, in its standard statement, holds that in an isolated system entropy never ___ over time (it either increases or stays the same).
explanation: The expected answer is 'decreases': the Second Law states that the entropy of an isolated system never decreases (ΔS ≥ 0), with equality only for reversible processes. This one-directional tendency toward higher-entropy states is the thermodynamic arrow of time, which the book treats as the most physically fundamental of the macroscopic arrows.
